title: The lore/quest release lockstep is only CHANGELOG prose -- nothing machine-checks that the pair moves together
description:
@opum-ai/quest and @opum-ai/lore have shipped as a version-matched pair since 0.5.0. Verified live while auditing pre-0.7.0 state (2026-09-14): quest and lore currently agree at 0.6.2 on every axis checked -- root package.json on dev and main for both repos, and the npm registry for both packages -- but that agreement is coincidental to the process, not enforced by it. Checked quest-cli side directly: package.json has no dependency or peerDependency on @opum-ai/lore at all. The pairing is stated only as prose (CHANGELOG entries, release notes, session handoffs) -- the exact shape of contract this release cycle exists to fix everywhere else (QCLI-289s contractVersion signal, QCLI-284s CI-hint sentence). The pairing rule itself is an unenforced contract.

Explicitly scoped post-0.7.0: do not fold this into the current release. Filed only so the gap is owned rather than living in cross-session message traffic.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A decision is recorded on whether and how to machine-check the lore/quest version pairing (a CI check comparing published versions, a manifest field, a paired-release script, or an explicit decision that prose is sufficient and why)
If a check is built, it fails closed (non-zero exit, no silent pass) when the two declared versions diverge without a recorded exception
The decision and its reasoning are recorded somewhere a future release will actually read (a decision record and/or the release runbook), not only on this task
